label: GO step, confidently choosing a2, after an unrewarded trial or late in the episode
explanation: Almost entirely a GO-phase unit (96% of mass at GO, essentially never at D2, a little at D1). It fires only when the agent is about to choose a2: 99.9% of mass has action == 2, and it is gated by a strongly a2-favoring policy logit (choice < -6). It never fires for a1 choices. Within a2 GO steps it fires mostly (1) after an unrewarded previous trial (prev_reward == 0; rate 0.097 vs 0.026 after reward), or (2) in the last ~15 trials of the episode (ep_trial 80-99 hold ~65% of mass), plus a small burst on the episode first trial. The largest activations are a2 GO steps after no reward, late in the episode, with low model value (value < 5.2 holds 55% of mass). Predicate uses only observed quantities: the model own policy logit at GO, the reward seen at D1, and trial position. The bare GO & a2 predicate has recall 0.98 but precision 0.28; adding the unrewarded-or-late condition raises F1 to 0.80 on dev. The ep_trial >= 85 cutoff is a fitted approximation of a smooth increase late in the episode.

issues: The verdict contradicts its own numbers. Test F1 is 0.793, under the 0.8 bar. Dev F1 is 0.7999, also just under. So 'explained' is not earned; at best this is partially_explained.

The 'small burst on the episode's first trial' is listed as a case 'among a2 GO steps', but it does not happen at GO. (ep_trial==0)&(phase==GO) has precision 0.0 (0 of 525 steps active). (ep_trial==0)&(phase==D1) has precision 1.0 and holds 3.9% of the mass. The burst is entirely at the first D1, and the predicate misses it. Adding it lifts dev F1 to 0.805 and mass recall to 0.986.

The 'unrewarded' branch hides a structure the predicate misses: rare vs common transition, and episode position. Among GO, choice<-6, trial<85, prev_reward==0 steps: after a rare previous transition precision is 0.66 (the profile shows rate 0.084 for prev_common==0 vs 0.038 for common). After a common one it is 0.53, falling to 0.30 for trials 40-84 (test). Unrewarded steps early in the episode (trial<40) have precision 0.87, but mid-episode (40-84) only 0.41. Most false positives are mid-episode GO a2 steps after a common-unrewarded trial, often while S1 is the good state.

The label and explanation never say the unit fires on a2 REPEATS, not on switches to a2. (GO)&(action==2)&(prev_action==1) has precision 0.004 and 0.04% of the mass; stay==0 has rate 0.001. In model-based terms it fires on a2 stays after rare-unrewarded trials (precision 0.69) and almost never after rare-rewarded ones (precision 0.037). That reads as 'staying with a2 despite no reward', not just 'unrewarded'.

The late-episode branch fires regardless of reward: trial>=85 & prev_reward==1 has precision 0.84. The value claim holds (value<5.2 holds 54% of the mass, precision 0.92), but value looks like a stand-in for time left in the episode. Unrewarded mid-episode steps with value<5.2 are essentially absent (20 steps).
